QF.id: XIII Sales Practices, Code of Conduct and Investor Protection_4

question.text: What is the grievance redressal escalation path for a derivative market investor?

answer.text: First approach the market participant / intermediary (trading member or broker); if unresolved, escalate to the exchange/MII or to SEBI through SCORES as applicable; if still unresolved, use Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for conciliation and, where required, arbitration
Direct complaint to SEBI → SAT → Supreme Court
There is no formal grievance mechanism — investors must approach consumer courts directly

explanation.text: The Logic: The investor first raises the complaint with the market participant/intermediary. If it is not satisfactorily resolved, the next step is the exchange/Market Infrastructure Institution or SCORES on the SEBI portal, depending on the nature of the complaint. Any remaining dispute can be taken to the SMART ODR portal for online conciliation and, if conciliation fails, online arbitration. The Trap: Going directly to SEBI or to courts without first using the intermediary and exchange/SCORES channels is not the prescribed path. RBI is not part of the grievance chain for exchange-traded derivatives. SMART ODR sits after the intermediary/exchange/SCORES layer, not before it. Note: Keep documented evidence (contract notes, order confirmations, written communications) at every stage — arbitration awards arising from ODR proceedings are binding and enforceable.
